observed_text: Tabulated coherence length ξ0: Al 1.6 μm, Sn 0.23 μm, Pb 0.090 μm, Nb 0.030 μm (a second table gives Nb 39 nm); YBCO ξ_ab 1.2–1.4 nm. Aluminium wires thinned from about 100 nm to below 10 nm still superconduct; quantum phase slips appear below about 50 nm and the wire crosses over to normal near 10 nm.
implied_text: A connected superconducting path is the buffer. ξ is a material length, not a minimum size: wires far thinner than ξ0 superconduct, and the measured size limit is a cross-section of order 10 nm reached through a rising phase-slip rate.
description: Superconductivity needs a connected path; the coherence length is a material property and not a minimum hardware size.
notes: value_si is Nb ξ0 = 30 nm from the review table. Closed-loop persistent current is owned by flux-quantization.

observed_text: Gap frequency 2Δ/h computed from tabulated gaps: Al 85 GHz, Sn 269 GHz, Pb 660 GHz, Nb 735 GHz.
implied_text: DC zero resistance is the ω→0 output of a gapped condensate that still has an internal clock at 2Δ/h.
description: The condensate clock sits near 10^11 Hz in conventional metals; laboratory DC is already slow compared with that scale.
notes: value_si is Al, the low end. This is not a voltage-standard lock; that lives on josephson-effect.

observed_text: Δ(0): Al 0.175 meV, Sn 0.557 meV, Pb 1.365 meV, Nb 1.52 meV. The ratio 2Δ(0)/kTc computed from the same table is 3.41, 3.47, 4.40 and 3.81; the weak-coupling BCS value is 3.52.
implied_text: 2Δ is the energy threshold that suppresses ordinary quasiparticle transport. kTc, μ0 Hc (or Hc2), and the specimen Ic are the macroscopic envelopes that close that gap.
description: Zero resistance is protected by a measured gap that vanishes at Tc; the BCS ratio is a fit, not a universal node rule.
notes: value_si is the BCS weak-coupling value. Pairing mechanisms are not QSA content.

observed_text: Tc: Al 1.19 K, Sn 3.73 K, Pb 7.2 K, Nb 9.25 K; Hg 4.15 K, NbTi 9.4 K, Nb3Sn 18 K; YBCO 92–93.7 K near optimal doping.
implied_text: T > Tc closes the gap and restores finite R.
description: Thermal collapse of zero-resistance transport at the material-specific critical temperature.
notes: Material numbers, not a single universal Tc. value_si is Nb. In wires below about 50 nm the transition broadens through phase slips.

observed_text: Type I at T→0: Al 10 mT, Sn 30.5 mT, Pb 80.3 mT. Nb at 2 K: Bc1 ≈ 160 mT, Bc2 ≈ 300 mT. NbTi Bc2 = 14 T. YBCO films, extrapolated: 153 T (field along c) and 638 T (in plane).
implied_text: H > Hc (type I) or H > Hc2 (type II) destroys the condensate and restores finite R. Between Hc1 and Hc2, complete field expulsion has already failed while R=0 can still hold if vortices are pinned.
description: Field collapse of the condensate sits at Hc or Hc2; Meissner can fail earlier without ending R=0.
value_text: H > Hc (10–80 mT, type I) or Hc2 (0.3 T Nb; 14 T NbTi)
notes: value_si is NbTi Bc2. This entry owns R=0; meissner owns expulsion. The YBCO values are a model extrapolation.

observed_text: The critical current is specimen-specific. Pinned NbTi carries 3700 A/mm² at 5 T and 4.2 K; without pinning a transport current moves the flux tubes and a flux-flow resistance appears.
implied_text: I > Ic produces dissipation by pair-breaking, hot spots, or flux flow. That is a current-budget failure of the coherent channel.
description: Zero resistance ends when the transport current exceeds the specimen Ic. There is no universal current number.
notes: No material constant is filed. Flux motion in the mixed state is a crossover owned jointly with type-ii-critical-field.

observed_text: DC resistance below the instrument floor; the decay time of a persistent current in a superconducting solenoid was bounded at more than 100,000 years.
implied_text: Stable R=0 transport, and a persistent loop current at zero continuous voltage, inside the T / H / I envelope.
description: Superconductivity owns the R=0 artifact. Holding a persistent current costs zero continuous voltage.
notes: The 100,000-year bound rests on a snippet of a secondary account of File and Mills (1963). Zero hold power is a convention: no voltage on the loop.

observed_text: The coherence length spans 0.3 nm to 1.6 μm across materials and is not a minimum size; pinning, which decides whether the mixed state is lossless, is set by microstructure.
implied_text: QSA does not have a single buffer number for the condensate, and it does not yet have a buffer/barrier specification for the pinning step that protects R=0 after Meissner has failed.
description: The T/H/I collapses are located; hardware identity and mixed-state pinning are recorded as gaps rather than filled.
notes: File-level mapping is Medium for these two gaps. This entry does not assert a pairing mechanism.

observed_text: Tabulated penetration depth: Al 16 nm, Sn 50 nm, Pb 40 nm, Nb 85 nm; a second table gives Pb 32 nm, Sn about 30 nm, Nb 32 nm (typical range 20–50 nm). YBCO: λa 103 nm, λb 80 nm, λc 635 nm. The field decays as exp(−x/λ) into a flat surface.
implied_text: λ is the e-folding depth of the field. A body several λ thick has a field-free interior; a thinner body screens partially and still superconducts.
description: Complete expulsion needs a screening buffer of tens of nanometres in conventional elements, of order 100 nm in YBCO's ab plane.
notes: value_si is Pb, 40 nm. The two opened tables differ by a factor of 2.7 for Nb. λ is not a minimum thickness for superconductivity.

observed_text: Expulsion on cooling through Tc is limited by thermal diffusion, eddy-current transients, and (in type II) flux-line motion — laboratory times, not the gap frequency 2Δ/h.
implied_text: This entry's static observation is the ω=0 expelled state. The gap frequency still sets the scale on which the condensate can respond to a changing field.
description: Static Meissner expulsion is not a 2Δ/h clock measurement; the expelled state is already the DC output.
notes: Contrast with josephson-effect, which owns the voltage-frequency lock.

observed_text: Type I: no field in the bulk below Hc (Al 10 mT, Sn 30.5 mT, Pb 80.3 mT). Type II: complete expulsion below Hc1 (Nb ≈ 160 mT at 2 K).
implied_text: Hc (type I) and Hc1 (type II) are the load-bearing field gates for complete expulsion. Holding the expelled state costs no continuous power.
description: Complete field expulsion is gated by Hc or Hc1, not by a static anisotropy latch.
value_text: H < Hc (type I; Pb 80.3 mT) or H < Hc1 (type II; Nb 160 mT)
notes: value_si is Pb μ0 Hc. Type-II Hc1 and the mixed state are owned by type-ii-critical-field.

observed_text: Above Hc (type I) the field enters and superconductivity ends; above Hc1 (type II) the field enters as flux tubes of one Φ0 while zero resistance can persist to Hc2. Pb 80.3 mT; Nb Bc1 ≈ 160 mT, Bc2 ≈ 300 mT at 2 K.
implied_text: Crossing the complete-expulsion gate is a Meissner failure even when the R=0 channel is still open.
description: The Meissner artifact dies at Hc or Hc1; that is not the same collapse as R=0.
value_text: H > Hc (type I) or H > Hc1 (type II)
notes: Split from superconductivity is required by the type-II mixed state. Hc2 is owned by type-ii-critical-field.

observed_text: In a sheet thinner than λ the field does not fall to zero at the centre and the sheet's critical field can be much larger than that of a thick slab; it remains superconducting. London slab: mid-plane field B0/cosh(d/2λ), 0.89 B0 at d = λ, 0.43 B0 at 3λ, 0.013 B0 at 10λ. One-atomic-layer Pb and In films superconduct.
implied_text: Screening weakens continuously as the body thins; there is no thickness at which expulsion switches off, and superconductivity is not lost at d = λ.
description: Expulsion is incomplete in a body thinner than a few λ; a crossover, not a minimum thickness.
notes: value_si is λ for Pb. The monolayer result rests on a snippet.

observed_text: Expulsion appears on cooling below Tc and ends on warming through it; the critical fields fall to zero at Tc.
implied_text: Thermal closure of the parent gap sends the screening depth to infinity and the expelled state disappears.
description: Expulsion ends at Tc with the parent condensate.
notes: Material Tc values are tabulated on superconductivity. Type-I intermediate state from a finite demagnetizing factor is a shape-dependent partition, not a second condensate.

observed_text: A superconducting element such as lead expels a weak magnetic field from its interior when cooled below Tc; the bulk field vanishes behind a surface layer of depth λ.
implied_text: A field-free interior behind a surface layer of depth λ is the stable output of a fully provisioned screening buffer.
description: Complete Meissner expulsion is perfect diamagnetism of the expelled volume, held at zero continuous power.
notes: This entry owns field expulsion / λ. Superconductivity owns R=0.

observed_text: Cooling in a field yields B=0 rather than freeze-in. A hypothetical perfect conductor would trap the flux it already contained, not expel it. λ is a measured screening length, not a derived node count.
implied_text: QSA records expulsion as the stable output of the gapped state; it does not yet produce expulsion-versus-trapping from a more primitive update rule, and it takes λ as the hardware depth.
description: Why the equilibrium is expulsion rather than flux trapping is located as data, not derived from node rules. That is a gap, not a contradiction.
notes: File-level mapping remains High. Same kind of underived screening length as the optical decay length λ/4πk on reflection.

observed_text: In Al/AlOx/Al junctions the oxide barrier is about 1 to 2 nm thick with a Gaussian spread, and less than 10 % of the barrier area dominates the tunnelling.
implied_text: Two nested buffers: each electrode must be a superconducting condensate, and they must be coupled by a weak link whose thickness sits in a narrow window. The load-bearing node of this artifact is the phase difference φ across that under-coupled spatial buffer.
description: The Josephson machine is a weak link, 1–2 nm of oxide in a tunnel junction, between two parent condensates; a thicker barrier carries less current.
notes: value_si is the middle of the measured 1–2 nm range. With no barrier the two sides are one superconductor with no junction degree of freedom. Electrode Tc, ξ and gap are owned by superconductivity.

observed_text: Josephson constant K_J = 2e/h = 483 597.848 4… GHz/V, exact since the 2019 SI: 483.6 MHz per microvolt.
implied_text: The AC Josephson lock is the clock: a microvolt bias oscillates at hundreds of megahertz; a millivolt bias sits in the sub-terahertz. This is a frequency locked to a voltage, not a plasma-period screening cycle.
description: The weak-link clock is 483.6 MHz per microvolt of DC bias.
notes: value_si is Hz per volt. Shapiro steps are the same clock read out against an external microwave drive.

observed_text: Ic is set by the junction (area, barrier transparency, electrode gap) and is not a universal constant. A DC supercurrent exists only for |I| ≤ Ic.
implied_text: Ic is the current threshold that protects the zero-voltage branch. The electrode gap is the energy scale that vanishes at Tc and takes Ic with it.
description: The zero-voltage branch is gated by a junction-specific Ic, not by a universal current.
notes: A flux of order Φ0 through the junction is a field threshold that suppresses Ic without first destroying the electrodes.

observed_text: The oxide barrier of a working Al junction is about 1 to 2 nm, and the thinnest tenth of its area carries most of the current, so the critical current falls steeply and continuously with thickness.
implied_text: A thicker insulator weakens the coupling continuously and the weak-link current falls toward zero.
description: A thicker or more opaque barrier is the spatial failure of the Josephson machine; a crossover in thickness.
notes: No decay length filed; the steep dependence is inferred from the dominance of the thinnest regions.

observed_text: Above Ic a finite DC voltage appears across the link. For |I| > Ic the junction is on a resistive branch and V ≠ 0.
implied_text: Current over-budget ends the zero-voltage branch. The voltage-frequency lock can then run; the dissipationless DC current is gone.
description: Crossing Ic collapses the V=0 supercurrent.
notes: T > Tc in either electrode is a coarser collapse: the parent condensate is gone. Electrode Hc / Hc2 is owned by superconductivity / type-ii-critical-field.

observed_text: A flux of order Φ0 = 2.067 833 848…×10⁻¹⁵ Wb through the junction area modulates Ic in a diffraction pattern with zeros at integer multiples of Φ0.
implied_text: A flux of order Φ0 is a field threshold that suppresses Ic without first destroying the electrodes.
description: Junction-scale flux of one quantum collapses Ic by interference, not by driving the electrodes normal.
notes: The diffraction pattern is cited to Rowell (1963), not opened. Φ0 is exact.

observed_text: V = (h/2e)ν with 2e/h = 483 597.848 4… GHz/V; under microwave irradiation at f the steps sit at V_n = n h f/2e (20.7 μV spacing at 10 GHz).
implied_text: The synchronized output is a universal voltage-frequency lock V = (h/2e) ν once a voltage is present, together with a dissipationless weak-link current at V=0 for |I| ≤ Ic.
description: The Josephson machine emits a metrological V–ν lock at 2e/h, and a zero-voltage supercurrent below Ic.
notes: Complementary metrological lock to quantum-hall-effect (RK = h/e²).

observed_text: The measured charge increment in h/2e is taken from the voltage-frequency lock and from the flux quantum.
implied_text: QSA does not derive why the increment is 2e rather than e from node rules alone. That increment is recorded as data. No pairing story is required to locate the collapses, and none is added.
description: The 2e in h/2e is located as a measured increment, not derived from node rules.
notes: File-level mapping remains High; the open item is the origin of the increment, not the location of the collapses. RSJ C and R are descriptive bookkeeping.

observed_text: The loop must be a closed superconducting path. A break, a normal section, or T > Tc anywhere on the circumference removes quantization of the trapped flux.
implied_text: A closed superconducting path is the hardware. The hole (or vortex core) is the region the condensate does not fill; the load-bearing buffer is the surrounding closed path.
description: Flux quantization requires a closed condensate path; an open ring is not this machine.
notes: The path must sit inside the superconductivity envelope. A vortex as the hole is owned by type-ii-critical-field.

observed_text: In a thick ring (wall thickness large compared with the London depth λ) the trapped flux itself is nΦ0. In a thin-walled cylinder the conserved quantity is the fluxoid; Little–Parks still has period Φ0.
implied_text: For the trapped flux (not merely the fluxoid) to sit at nΦ0, the wall must be thick enough that screening currents live in a surface layer of depth λ and the interior supercurrent vanishes.
description: Wall thickness versus λ selects flux integers versus fluxoid integers; both are the same constraint in two buffer regimes.
notes: A wall thinner than λ still fixes the fluxoid. λ values are on meissner. The Little–Parks period is cited to a letter that was not opened.

observed_text: There is no voltage-frequency lock on a fully superconducting loop at rest (V=0 around the path). A SQUID reads the same integer against the Josephson clock of the interrupting junctions.
implied_text: The relevant latency is the screening response of the parent condensate (London / plasma scales on meissner), not a Josephson oscillation of the loop itself.
description: A quiet superconducting loop holds n at V=0; it does not run the 483.6 MHz/μV clock until a weak link is inserted.
notes: Cross-cite josephson-effect for the SQUID readout clock.

observed_text: The stored integer changes by a phase slip: the order parameter goes to zero at one point of the path and the phase jumps by 2πn, with a voltage pulse. Quantum phase slips are measurable in wires below about 50 nm and dominate near 10 nm.
implied_text: Changing the stored integer by one requires a phase slip: a local collapse of the gap on the loop, or a vortex crossing the wall. That barrier keeps n fixed and vanishes if any section is driven normal, or if T → Tc.
description: The stored integer is a latch: a phase-slip barrier protects n at zero continuous power.
notes: Contrast with bose-einstein-condensate, which is not held at zero continuous power.

observed_text: Opening the ring, driving a section normal, or a lead / normal gap on the circumference releases the constraint and the integer condition disappears.
implied_text: Topology failure: if the path is not closed, the fluxoid is not conserved and there is no trapped integer.
description: A broken loop cannot hold nΦ0.
notes: Electrode-scale H > Hc or Hc2 destroys the path itself.

observed_text: Warming the loop through Tc releases the constraint and the integer condition disappears.
implied_text: Thermal collapse of the parent condensate erases the fluxoid latch.
description: The trapped integer dies with the superconducting path at Tc.
notes: Material Tc values live on superconductivity. A weak spot or a current near the loop Ic lets n step without shifting Φ0.

observed_text: The flux through a superconducting ring is quantized in units of Φ0 = h/2e = 2.067 833 848…×10⁻¹⁵ Wb (exact since 2019).
implied_text: A trapped fluxoid equal to nΦ0, held at zero continuous power for as long as the loop, the gap, and the phase-slip barrier remain inside the envelope.
description: The machine's stable product is the integer fluxoid n h/2e.
notes: Combined with the AC Josephson lock this is the same constant in a different geometry. Chargeless analog is h/m4 on superfluid-helium-4.

observed_text: The single-valuedness relation uses q=2e as the measured charge increment. Φ0 = h/2e is a defined SI combination taken from that increment.
implied_text: The 2e in h/2e is taken from the measured quantum, not derived from node rules. No pairing story is added to close it.
description: Same open charge increment as on josephson-effect; the integer condition itself is not in doubt.
notes: File-level mapping remains High. λ and ξ that set how small a hole or vortex core can be are owned by meissner and type-ii-critical-field.

observed_text: Type II when κ = λ/ξ > 1/√2. From tabulated lengths: Al 0.010, Sn 0.22, Pb 0.44, Nb 2.8 (0.82 from a second table).
implied_text: Three nested spatial scales are required before this artifact exists as something other than a type-I Meissner state: ξ (core), λ (screening cloud), and the condition λ > ξ/√2.
description: Type II is the regime in which the screening cloud outruns the coherence-length core.
notes: λ is shared with meissner; ξ is the core size that closes at Hc2. This file owns the mixed-state window.

observed_text: The flux tubes form a triangular lattice with spacing √(2Φ0/√3B): 49 nm at 1 T and 20 nm at 6 T. Each tube carries one Φ0 and has a normal core of area about πξ².
implied_text: Vortex lattice spacing is an extra, field-tuned buffer that has no type-I counterpart. The mixed state is a synchronized array of these defects, not a uniform condensate.
description: At tesla-scale B the mixed-state lattice is a tens-of-nanometres array of Φ0 tubes.
value_text: d = √(2Φ0/√3B): 49 nm at 1 T, 20 nm at 6 T
notes: value_si is √(Φ0/1 T) from the stated Φ0. Spacing tracks the field; it is not a material constant.

observed_text: Screening and core adjustment follow the parent-condensate electromagnetic / gap clocks (London / plasma scales; gap frequency). Flux-flow voltages, when present, sit on a much slower, geometry- and drive-dependent scale set by vortex velocity.
implied_text: This entry is not a voltage-standard clock; that lock lives on josephson-effect.
description: Mixed-state dynamics inherit the parent condensate clocks; flux flow is a slower, non-universal scale.
notes: Not the 483.6 MHz/μV lock.

observed_text: Nb at 2 K: Bc1 ≈ 160 mT, Bc2 ≈ 300 mT. NbTi Bc2 = 14 T. YBCO films, extrapolated: 153 T and 638 T.
implied_text: Hc1 is the field threshold for first entry of a Φ0 defect. Hc2 is the field threshold that closes the gap. Pinning sites supply an additional barrier against vortex motion; that barrier protects the zero-resistance reading and is not the same threshold as Hc2.
description: The mixed-state window is the field interval between first vortex entry and gap closure.
value_text: Hc1 < H < Hc2 (Nb 0.16–0.30 T; NbTi to 14 T)
notes: NbTi and Nb3Sn remain superconducting in tesla-scale fields at liquid-helium temperature; YBCO does so at liquid-nitrogen temperature, with a strongly anisotropic Hc2. Specific tesla numbers live on superconductivity.

observed_text: Above Hc2 the cores overlap and the sample is normal: Nb ≈ 0.30 T at 2 K, NbTi 14 T.
implied_text: H > Hc2 destroys the ξ-buffer, closes the gap, and ends this artifact.
description: Upper-critical-field collapse is gap destruction, not first penetration.
notes: Collapse at Hc1 is a collapse of meissner, not of the gap. Treating them as one critical field would hide the vortex-lattice buffer.

observed_text: A transport current through an unpinned type-II conductor in a field moves the flux tubes and produces a flux-flow resistance; pinning centres prevent it. Pinned NbTi carries 3700 A/mm² at 5 T and 4.2 K.
implied_text: Free vortex motion is a failure of the R=0 artifact while the gap and the lattice are still present. That is a different collapse from Hc2.
description: Unpinned flux flow dumps dissipation into the mixed state without closing the gap.
notes: Owned jointly with superconductivity, which owns R=0. Pinning landscape is the consistency-gap row.

observed_text: Between Hc1 and Hc2 flux enters as a triangular lattice of tubes, each carrying one flux quantum Φ0 = h/2e = 2.067 833 848…×10⁻¹⁵ Wb; the lattice is imaged by decorating a niobium surface with iron particles.
implied_text: A mixed state whose field scale is set by ξ and λ, whose flux is packaged as an integer number of Φ0 tubes, and whose lattice spacing is √(2Φ0/√3B), for as long as Hc1 < H < Hc2 and T < Tc.
description: The stable output is a field-tuned lattice of Φ0 phase defects.
notes: Same quantum as flux-quantization: a vortex is a phase defect that plays the role of the hole.

observed_text: Pinning — the barrier that decides whether the mixed state is dissipationless — is set by microstructure (precipitates, grain boundaries, irradiation defects) and is not a universal function of λ and ξ.
implied_text: QSA does not yet have a clean buffer/barrier specification for that mesoscale step. The Hc1 / Hc2 / κ collapses do not depend on closing it.
description: Mixed-state classification is closed; the pinning landscape that protects R=0 is still underived, of the same kind as mesoscale coercivity.
notes: File-level mapping remains High. Same class of gap as permanent-magnet-latch coercivity. Superconductivity records the R=0 side of this gap.

observed_text: A connected volume of liquid 4He below Tλ, large enough to support a nonzero ρs. Superflow through packed powder and fine capillaries, and a climbing film, are the macroscopic demonstrations. There is no charge, no London λ, and no Meissner expulsion.
implied_text: The condensate buffer is a connected superfluid volume. The superleak or film is apparatus that the normal fraction cannot pass — a spatial filter, not the condensate buffer. Quantized circulation requires a closed path.
description: Chargeless superflow needs connected 4He with ρs > 0; it does not need an electromagnetic screening depth.
notes: Vortex cores are the chargeless analog of mixed-state defects. Do not collapse this hardware with dilute alkali BECs.

observed_text: There is no Josephson voltage-frequency lock (no e). Weak-link apertures in helium do produce an analogous current-phase oscillation; that is a related observation, not the primary artifact here. Second sound is a temperature wave in the two-fluid bookkeeping.
implied_text: Second sound is a hydrodynamic clock of the already formed superfluid, not the clock that opens the λ-point.
description: Superfluid 4He has no 2e/h lock; its internal hydro clock is not the Tλ specification.
value_text: no 2e/h lock; second sound is hydro
notes: Aperture analog belongs here as a related observation; the electrical specifications stay on josephson-effect.

observed_text: Tλ = 2.1768 K at saturated vapour pressure. The superfluid fraction goes continuously to zero there, ρs/ρ ∝ (1 − T/Tλ)^0.6717.
implied_text: Tλ is the thermal threshold: ρs vanishes and the superflow responses go with it.
description: The load-bearing thermal gate of chargeless superflow is the λ-point at 2.1768 K.
notes: Value at saturated vapour pressure; the pressure dependence has no opened source. Two-fluid language is bookkeeping of ρs(T), not two substances.

observed_text: Above Tλ = 2.1768 K the superfluid fraction is zero and the liquid is an ordinary viscous fluid.
implied_text: T > Tλ sets ρs = 0 and ends every superfluid response.
description: Thermal collapse of chargeless superflow at 2.1768 K.
notes: Solidification across the melting curve is a coarser hardware removal.

observed_text: Landau critical velocity for roton creation, from ion drift: about 60 m/s at saturated vapour pressure, 46 m/s at 24 bar. Critical velocities in apertures and channels are lower, fall in two regimes, are not reproducible between experiments, and in small apertures reflect thermally activated vortex nucleation.
implied_text: The velocity limit has a sharp upper bound (roton emission) and a lower, statistical limit set by vortex nucleation over a barrier.
description: Superflow has a velocity limit inside the T < Tλ envelope: a sharp Landau bound and a lower, channel-dependent statistical limit.
value_text: v > vc: ≤ 60 m/s (Landau); lower and geometry-dependent in channels
notes: value_si is the Landau bound. The channel limit is a crossover; the Landau bound is a threshold.

observed_text: Circulation quantum h/m4 = 9.97×10⁻⁸ m²/s, computed from the exact Planck constant and the helium-4 atomic mass; single quanta are observed building up in aperture flow.
implied_text: The chargeless counterpart of Φ0 is the circulation quantum h/m4 on a closed path.
description: Superfluid 4He emits an integer winding with measured quantum h/m4.
notes: Cross-check with flux-quantization is the existence of an integer winding, not identity of the two constants.

observed_text: Persistent currents circulate in a closed torus on laboratory timescales. Viscosity through a fine channel → 0 for the superfluid fraction below Tλ.
implied_text: Stable chargeless superflow and a persistent circulating integer at zero continuous power, inside T < Tλ and v < vc.
description: Holding superflow costs zero watts. The fountain and superleak responses are the same dissipationless output.
notes: Fountain head and vanishing viscosity are the same machine class. Contrast with BEC, which needs continuous cooling and trapping.

observed_text: The load-bearing collapse is loss of ρs at Tλ (and of superflow at vc), not a measured charge gap of the superconducting kind. Why the λ-point sits at 2.1768 K is not derived from node rules; the ideal-gas formula at the liquid density gives 3.15 K.
implied_text: The family name gapped is slightly loose here. The assignment follows the taxonomy rule — protected collective mode with a critical temperature — not a pairing-gap identification.
description: Chargeless superflow sits in gapped-coherence by collapse type, not by a pairing gap. The numerical origin of Tλ is also open.
notes: File-level mapping remains High. Two-fluid bookkeeping is not used to derive Tλ. Dense interacting 4He is not the same hardware as a dilute alkali BEC.

observed_text: Ideal-gas threshold n λT³ = ζ(3/2) ≃ 2.612 at the centre of the trap; kTc = 0.94 ħω N^(1/3). The measured transition is very close to this value. Sodium at 2 μK needs 1.5×10¹⁴ cm⁻³, as measured.
implied_text: The nodes are the atoms; the buffer is the combination of number, volume, and temperature that puts enough of them in one mode. This is the measured phase-space condition taken as the specification, not a derived node rule.
description: A trapped cloud becomes a condensate when its phase-space density crosses the ideal-gas value 2.612.
notes: Envelope/relabel of the ideal-gas condition, not a derived node rule. In a harmonic trap the same condition at peak density gives Tc that scales as N^{1/3} times the trap frequency.

observed_text: Atom numbers range from a few thousand to several million; about 300 nK for 40,000 atoms; sodium condensates of up to 5×10⁵ atoms below about 2 μK.
implied_text: A working envelope of the apparatus class. There is no minimum atom number at which the effect switches on; the transition is rounded in a finite system.
description: The laboratory node count is a working envelope, not a derived minimum.
notes: value_si is a geometric mid-class of the quoted atom-number window. Species-by-species scattering lengths and interaction Tc shifts are medium and are not required here.

observed_text: Trap frequencies set the sloshing / expansion clocks of the cloud; they are apparatus scales, not a universal condensate clock. There is no Josephson 2e/h lock and no cyclotron clock. Interaction-driven sound in the condensed cloud is a hydrodynamic response of an already-formed condensate.
implied_text: The BEC has no metrological lock and no material gap frequency; its clocks are trap and hydro scales of an already condensed cloud.
description: Laboratory BEC clocks are apparatus and hydro, not a universal condensate tick.
notes: Analogous to second sound on superfluid-helium-4.

observed_text: The condensate fraction, 1 − (T/Tc)³ in a harmonic trap, falls to zero at Tc, or as the density is lowered through n λT³ = 2.612 at fixed T. This is not an anisotropy barrier and not a pairing gap.
implied_text: The load-bearing threshold is thermal / density. Holding the condensate requires continuous cooling and trapping resources; it is not a zero-power latch.
description: BEC is gated by Tc(n), not by a pairing gap or a remanence barrier.
value_text: T > Tc(n) or n dropped at fixed T
notes: Contrast with permanent-magnet-latch and flux-quantization, which hold state at zero continuous power.

observed_text: Above Tc(n) the condensate fraction, 1 − (T/Tc)³ in a harmonic trap, is zero; a sudden onset is measured at T/Tc ≈ 1.
implied_text: T > Tc(n) destroys macroscopic occupation and phase coherence.
description: Thermal collapse of the condensate fraction at the density-set Tc.
notes: Working Tc sits in the nK–μK class of the apparatus envelope. Heating and three-body loss are practical routes to this collapse, not a third machine class.

observed_text: The condition n λT³ = 2.612 can be crossed by lowering the density at fixed temperature. When the trap is switched off the cloud expands; the narrow peak and the interference fringes are imaged during that expansion, which also ends the sample.
implied_text: Atom loss or a weaker trap lowers n through the critical line at fixed T, the same collapse as warming. Without confinement the cloud is not a lasting laboratory condensate, although release is also the readout step.
description: A fall in density walks the cloud back through nλT³ ≈ 2.612.
notes: Same critical line as the hardware-scale row; this row is the density-drop failure.

observed_text: A sharp peak on the thermal distribution, imaged after the trap is switched off, and interference between two condensates. A stirred condensate heats only above a critical velocity, and flow in a toroidal trap persists for up to 10 s.
implied_text: The stable output is a macroscopic occupation of one mode — read as a condensate fraction, a narrow velocity peak, and interference contrast — only while the cloud stays above the critical phase-space density.
description: The machine's product is one-mode occupation and interference contrast, not a quantized electrical constant.
notes: No claim is made about what the condensate is. Relation to superfluid-helium-4 is analogical.

observed_text: An ideal-gas BEC has no measured pairing gap. Collapse is loss of macroscopic occupation and of phase coherence, not gap closure of the superconducting kind. N ~ 10^3–10^7 is a working envelope, not a derived minimum node count. The laboratory condensate is not held at zero continuous power.
implied_text: The file sits in gapped-coherence because the taxonomy groups protected collective modes that die at a critical temperature. Forcing a gap onto the alkali cloud would be an interpretive overlay. QSA takes 2.612 from the ideal-gas condition.
description: Family assignment is looser than a pairing gap; the thermal/density threshold is real, the gap language is not, and the phase-space threshold is taken rather than derived.
notes: File-level mapping is Medium for this tension, the absence of a minimum node count, and the taken 2.612. A dilute condensate is a superfluid by direct test (critical velocity, persistent flow); dense 4He differs in density and interaction strength.

observed_text: The effect is observed in a two-dimensional electron gas at low temperature and high field (Si MOSFET, GaAs/AlGaAs at 0.1 K, graphene at 300 K and 29–45 T). The orbital quantization depends solely on the field component normal to the plane.
implied_text: A two-dimensional electron buffer plus a field component normal to it is the measured architecture; a single atomic layer is enough. Once the field opens a gap in the bulk of the sheet, the remaining current path is along the edges. QSA records this layered hardware; it does not derive the edge path from node rules.
description: Integer quantum Hall plateaus need a two-dimensional electron system and a normal field component; a 3D metal is the wrong buffer.
notes: Magnetic length ℓB = √(ℏ/eB⊥): 25.7 nm at 1 T, 8.1 nm at 10 T.

observed_text: The cyclotron frequency ωc = eB/m is the field-set clock. ħωc is the Landau-level spacing. The Hall plateau is not itself a radiated frequency; it is a DC resistance that remains stable while that clock keeps the Landau ladder resolved against scattering and against kT.
implied_text: The same eB/m combination that cyclotron-resonance reads as an absorption line is here the clock that keeps the gap resolved so a DC plateau can exist.
description: QHE runs on a cyclotron clock; the output is a resistance plateau, not an absorption line.
notes: Cross-cite cyclotron-resonance, which owns the line.

observed_text: Graphene: Landau gap 2820 K at 45 T (9.4 kT at 300 K), measured activation energy about 600 K. Conventional semiconductors had not shown the effect above 30 K.
implied_text: The Landau-level (mobility) gap is the energy barrier that protects a plateau. The perpendicular-field condition is a field threshold that opens the gap; moving B so that ν sits between integers takes the system out of a gap.
description: A plateau is a gap-protected DC state: kT or a Hall field comparable to the gap collapses the quantization.
notes: Disorder that widens a plateau is a sample-dependent resource, analogous to pinning on type-ii-critical-field. Integer values of RH do not depend on closing it; the width of the flat region does.

observed_text: With the field tilted up to 90° from the normal, the magneto-oscillations of a silicon inversion layer depend solely on the normal component B cos θ; the parallel component has a negligible effect on the orbital quantization.
implied_text: Tilting lowers the gap continuously; an in-plane field is the zero of that dependence, not a separate switch.
description: The plateaus follow the normal field component; an in-plane field gives none.
value_text: gap follows B cos θ; zero in-plane
notes: Established in 1968 (Fang and Stiles). Distinct from moving a normal field off a plateau.

observed_text: Off a plateau the longitudinal resistance is finite and the Hall resistance is not flat; the deviation of the Hall resistance is linear in the longitudinal resistivity. Plateaus are centred where ν = ns h/(eB⊥) is near an integer.
implied_text: When ν is not in a gap, the protected edge-channel output is gone.
description: Off-integer filling is the field/filling collapse of the plateau.
notes: Filling ν locates the plateaus; it is bookkeeping, not a derivation of RH = h/νe². Plateau width is set by disorder and temperature.

observed_text: A high current or a raised temperature gives a finite longitudinal resistivity, and the deviation of the Hall resistance from its quantized value is linear in that resistivity. Activation energy about 600 K in graphene at 29–45 T.
implied_text: Thermal population of adjacent levels, or Hall-field / current breakdown, collapses the gap protection. Buffer destruction is a coarser failure of the same machine.
description: High T or high current wash the plateaus out by overrunning the Landau/mobility gap.
value_text: kT or Hall field vs gap
notes: Graphene's high-temperature integer plateaus sit on the same gap-versus-kT clause and do not require a second family.

observed_text: RH = RK/i with RK = h/e² = 25 812.807 45… Ω (exact since 2019); independent of host material, device and plateau number to a few parts in 10¹⁰.
implied_text: A Hall resistance locked to RK/ν together with a vanishing longitudinal resistance, while the 2DEG, the perpendicular field, the temperature, and the current remain inside the envelope.
description: The stable metrological output is RH = h/νe² with Rxx → 0.
notes: Complementary lock to josephson-effect (2e/h). Fractional plateaus are a harder related case and are not the primary artifact.

observed_text: QSA takes RH = h/νe² from metrology. Filling ν = ns h/(eB) is bookkeeping, not a derivation of why RH equals that combination. Bulk gap plus edge path is the measured surviving hardware.
implied_text: QSA does not obtain h/e² from a node-count or buffer rule, and it does not yet specify why current is expelled to the edge and why that forces RH onto RK/ν. Fractional plateaus are explicitly unmapped.
description: The quantized Hall resistance is a universal output taken from metrology, not derived from node rules. That missing derivation is load-bearing.
notes: File-level mapping is Medium. Same class of gap as taking the optical decay length λ/4πk as given on reflection, but here the output is a universal constant. No anyon or fractional-charge story is added.

observed_text: Turning height of the lowest state 13.7 μm (computed, Airy solution); a slit lower than about 15 μm between mirror and absorber passes no neutrons. Horizontal velocity 5–15 m/s, vertical below 5 cm/s; mirrors 6–10 cm long.
implied_text: The spatial buffer is the height of the gravitational well above a reflecting floor.
description: A neutron with centimetre-per-second vertical speed, a horizontal mirror and g over about 14 μm is the hardware.

observed_text: Classical bounce period of the lowest state 3.3 ms; a 10 cm mirror at 10 m/s is crossed in 10 ms, about three periods.
implied_text: Not a nuclear lifetime.
description: UCN bounce clock.

observed_text: Level energies 1.4, 2.5, 3.3 and 4.1 peV (computed here: 1.41, 2.46, 3.32, 4.08 peV); E1/k = 16 nK.
implied_text: Gravitational level spacing is the protecting gap. Family name gapped is loose.
description: peV gravitational ladder, not a pairing gap.
notes: value_si corrected: 1.41 peV is 2.25×10⁻³¹ J (the earlier row was a factor of 1000 high).

observed_text: A slit lower than about 15 μm is not transparent to neutrons (count rate zero, reproduced 11 times); the ideal turning height is 13.7 μm and the fitted heights sit about 3 μm above the ideal values.
implied_text: Under-height slit or wrong buffer collapses the steps.
description: z < z1 or not-UCN is the collapse.
notes: Resolved to a few micrometres; the edge is softened by the overlap with the absorber.

observed_text: Zero transmission through a slit lower than about 15 μm and a rise above it; the computed turning heights of the first four states are 13.7, 24.0, 32.4 and 39.8 μm.
implied_text: Discrete gravitational states as the stable output.
description: Height steps at the Airy turning points.

observed_text: The spacing is gravitational, not a pairing gap. No charge, no λ, no Tc.
implied_text: Do not fold into gapped-condensate. Same honesty as He-4.
description: Family name is loose; leftover, not a tenth design.

observed_text: A constriction in a GaAs–AlGaAs electron gas with an opening comparable to the Fermi wavelength (about 45 nm, from sixteen steps at 360 nm) and much smaller than the mean free path.
implied_text: 1D saddle in a 2DEG is the buffer. A wide 3D metal is the wrong hardware.
description: QPC needs a ballistic ~λF constriction.

observed_text: Fermi-velocity transit through the saddle. The staircase is DC.
implied_text: Not a cyclotron clock and not a Hall plateau clock.
description: Transit clock; DC output.

observed_text: 1D subband edges open one by one. Pinch-off closes the last mode. No pairing gap and no Landau gap.
implied_text: Subband edges are the gates.
description: Mode edges, not 2Δ and not ħωc.

observed_text: Pinch-off gives zero conductance. The steps smear when the thermal energy approaches the mode spacing, and backscattering lowers each transmission below 1 (about 1 % deviation in a clean device).
implied_text: Last-mode close, thermal smear, or lost ballistic buffer collapse the staircase.
description: Pinch-off / T / mfp are the collapses.
notes: Pinch-off is a threshold; thermal smearing and scattering are crossovers.

observed_text: Conductance steps of 2e²/h = 7.748 091 729…×10⁻⁵ S with no magnetic field applied, up to sixteen steps, accurate to about 1 %.
implied_text: Taken Landauer output. Not RH = h/νe².
description: Two-terminal conductance steps at 2e²/h.

observed_text: The steps were measured with no magnetic field applied. The output is a two-terminal conductance of 2e²/h per mode, accurate to about 1 %, against parts in 10¹⁰ for the Hall resistance. The 0.7 feature is out of scope.
implied_text: Do not mint a tenth design that swallows QHE and QPC.
description: QPC is not QHE. 2e²/h is taken.
